FOLLOW-UP ADJUDICATION — Replace the current bare pivotality premise by a named, checkable “geodesic-core revealment and anti-concentration” (GRAC) condition, and make pivotality a lemma. For endpoint score-support blocks S_i(r),S_j(r), require a revealment algorithm which, off an error event of probability ζ₂(ℓ,r), exposes a canonical i–j geodesic as endpoint delays A_i,A_j (|A_i|+|A_j|≤Cr) plus a core passage count L_{ij} independent of the two endpoint blocks. If F_{ℓ,r} is the conditional cdf of L_{ij}, require the discrete-curvature bound
|Δ_uΔ_v F_{ℓ,r}(t)| ≤ C(|u|+1)(|v|+1)ℓ⁻¹ exp{−c(t−μℓ)²/ℓ}+ζ₂(ℓ,r),
and, for two selectors with four endpoint blocks, the analogous fourth mixed-difference bound C∏ₐ(|uₐ|+1)(ℓ₁ℓ₂)⁻¹ times a bivariate Gaussian envelope, except when their revealed corridors overlap. Require the normalized number/probability of overlapping-corridor quadruples plus the summed ζ₄ errors to vanish. These are properties of a shortest-path revealment/transfer kernel, not of scores, Q_n, R_n, Ω, or HAC.
Amend def:endpoint-pivotality accordingly: Δ₂ and Δ₄ should be the signed mixed-endpoint coefficients (suprema over centered, L^{4+δ}-normalized functions of the 2 or 4 endpoint blocks), not sums of absolute one-endpoint selector-change probabilities. Centering kills zeroth- and first-order endpoint effects, so total pivotal probability can stay nonzero and is unnecessarily strong. Add lem:GRAC-implies-pivotality: summing the Gaussian front over separations gives
Δ₂,n ≤ C[r_n²/√b_n + Z₂,n(r_n) + shell(b_n)ρ^{r_n}],
Δ₄,n ≤ C[r_n⁴/b_n + N₄,n(b_n)/n² + Z₄,n(r_n) + shell(b_n)²ρ^{r_n}],
with the same bounds uniformly for a family having common GRAC constants. Here Z₂,Z₄ are the declared summed revealment-failure bounds and N₄ counts overlapping revealed corridors. The proof is endpoint resampling + conditional centering + the displayed second/fourth cdf differences; the ℓ-sum of the Gaussian front is O(√b_n), and Hölder handles score truncation. Endpoint-quadratic then consumes this lemma, not a primitive Δ→0 assumption.
Local-chord verification is explicit. For ambient separation ℓ, shortest-path length is ℓ minus the maximum matching size in the Bernoulli word B_i,…,B_{j−2}; the two-state matching recursion is an irreducible aperiodic finite-state Markov-additive chain. Its transfer matrix gives uniformly sup_k P(D_ℓ=k)=O(ℓ⁻¹/²), sup_k|P(D_ℓ=k+1)−P(D_ℓ=k)|=O(ℓ⁻¹), and the corresponding two-distance fourth-difference bound. More strongly, on the cycle once b_n<n/4, the unique short-arc selector never reveals the terminal B_j, while h_j=B_j−1/2; hence the two-root centered coefficient is exactly zero for distinct endpoints. Each selected pair is supported on an arc of O(b_n) sites; among O(nb_n) pair summands each overlaps only O(b_n²) other pair corridors, so Δ₄,n=O(b_n³/n). Thus with b_n=⌊log(n+1)⌋ take r_n=⌈A log log(n+3)⌉ (replace the current 3log₂n choice): the general GRAC receipts are Δ₂=O((loglog n)²/√log n) and Δ₄=O((loglog n)⁴/log n+(log n)³/n), while the witness-specific revealment sharpens Δ₂ to 0 and Δ₄ to O((log n)³/n). Score truncation is actually zero for r_n≥2.
A genuinely applied covered class is the bounded-range Newman–Watts/finite-range small-world graph on a ring or fixed-width strip: deterministic nearest-neighbor backbone plus independent optional shortcuts of lengths 2,…,R with probabilities bounded away from 0 and 1. The R=2 one-dimensional member is exactly the supplied local-chord witness.
